title: Tamsin and the Typewriter
premise: In the river city of Vellham, on the eve of a revolution, Beatrix Eastwick works quietly in her late father's print shop, cutting typefaces and keeping her head down. When a census taker named Tamsin arrives asking questions about who owns what — and who really wrote the pamphlets that lit the city's unrest — Beatrix is drawn into a race to set the true history of the uprising in type before the victors' historians can burn or rewrite it. As the river ice groans toward its spring break, Beatrix and Tamsin hide the press, forge alliances with printers, soldiers, and street children, and discover that memory itself is contested territory. The book ends with the ice breaking: the original plates smuggled downriver to safety, the shop lost to fire, and Beatrix choosing to sign her father's name and her own to the record, claiming belonging at last.
about_author: Coral Okonkwo is a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in riverside mill towns. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to credit, and teaches a yearly workshop on setting type by hand.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A day in the Eastwick print shop: sorting type, mending the press, avoiding the neighborhood's growing unrest. She reveals her habit of hiding — in work, in routine. Emotional beat: quiet grief for her father, whose death left her invisible in a trade of loud men.

chapters.title: Questions on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Tamsin, a census taker with ink-stained cuffs and too many questions, arrives to count the household. They linger over the presses, noticing pamphlets Beatrix swears she knows nothing about. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; two people who both survive by observing others.

chapters.title: What the Census Wants
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We learn Tamsin is not merely counting heads — a ministry clerk has ordered them to log who prints seditious material. Tamsin hesitates, sensing the list will become a death warrant. Emotional beat: first crack in their official loyalty.

chapters.title: Pamphlets in the Snow
chapters.summary: Beatrix finds a bundle of anonymous pamphlets tucked in her father's old type case — his hand, his typeface, printed after his death. Someone is using the shop at night. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into resolve; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Beatrix stakes out the shop and catches a young printer's apprentice, Wren, setting type by candlelight. Wren confesses: her father was part of a secret circle of printers who documented the governor's abuses. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared inheritance.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Grievances
chapters.summary: Wren shows Beatrix the circle's ledger — names, confiscated letters, testimony from prisoners. Half the pages are missing, seized in a raid. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the weight of being keeper of other people's truths.

chapters.title: The Ministry Historian
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin meets Aldous Crane, the victors' appointed historian, who coolly explains which version of events will be 'on the record.' Tamsin realizes the census data feeds Crane's erasures. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; complicity becomes personal.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Crane visits the print shop, offering Beatrix protection and a government commission if she surrenders her father's typefaces as 'evidence.' She declines, heart pounding. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance; she understands the stakes now.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Winter deepens; the frozen river that carries the city's commerce becomes a symbol and a deadline — when it breaks, barges leave, and so will any chance to move the archive unseen. Emotional beat: claustrophobic patience, time ticking underfoot.

chapters.title: Tamsin Returns Off Duty
chapters.summary: Tamsin comes to the shop unofficially, warning Beatrix that her name has been flagged. They strike a fragile bargain: Tamsin will misfile the census entry if Beatrix helps them understand what the ledger means. Emotional beat: trust tentatively extended across enemy lines.

chapters.title: Reading the Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Together they reconstruct the seized pages from memory, proofs, and marginalia. Tamsin's clerical training proves invaluable; Beatrix recognizes her father's hand in corrections. Emotional beat: intimacy through collaboration; grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Wren's Mistake
chapters.summary: Wren prints a broadside too soon, drawing soldiers to the district. Beatrix hides the ledger inside a false bottom of the type cabinet as boots pound the stairs. Emotional beat: terror, then fury — and a hard lesson about carelessness.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: A captain questions Beatrix while soldiers search. She plays the timid tradeswoman, hands busy mending a forme, lying fluently for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: the cost of deception; she is no longer the woman who keeps her head down.

chapters.title: The Printer's Circle, Reassembled
chapters.summary: Beatrix tracks surviving members of her father's circle: a blind compositor, a tavern-keeper, an exiled foreman. Each holds a fragment. Emotional beat: bittersweet reunion; inheritance revealed as something built by many hands.

chapters.title: What Father Buried
chapters.summary: Following her father's typographic habits — a kerned ligature, a reversed 'e' — Beatrix decodes a hidden compartment in the press bed containing the master plates of the true account. Emotional beat: communion with the dead; her father trusted her all along.

chapters.title: Crane Closes In
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Crane grows suspicious of Tamsin's filings and assigns them to catalog the seized print shops — including Eastwick's. Tamsin must sabotage their own assignment without being caught. Emotional beat: dread of exposure; loyalty now fully transferred.

chapters.title: A Forged Inventory
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Beatrix fabricate a plausible inventory listing the plates as melted scrap. The forgery must be perfect — paper, seals, even the smell of officialdom. Emotional beat: exhilarating competence; the counterfeiter's thrill of making truth out of lies.

chapters.title: The Tavern Council
chapters.summary: The circle meets to plan moving the archive downriver before the ice breaks. Old grudges surface — some want to publish immediately, martyring themselves. Emotional beat: fractious solidarity; the difficulty of agreeing on what memory owes the living.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Compositor's
chapters.summary: The blind compositor is arrested; someone talked. Beatrix realizes the raid pattern points to a mole within the circle. Emotional beat: paranoia and heartbreak; trust, once broken, must be rebuilt piece by piece.

chapters.title: Suspicions
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Tamsin quietly test each member. Evidence points to the exiled foreman — or does Crane want them to think so? Emotional beat: the corrosive logic of suspicion, resisted only by choosing to believe.

chapters.title: The Mole Confesses
chapters.summary: The foreman admits he broke under torture threats but fed Crane only half-truths, protecting the plates' location. He offers to run decoy errands. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a strategic and moral act; broken things still bearing weight.

chapters.title: First Thaw
chapters.summary: A warm wind; the river begins to creak. The circle accelerates plans. Beatrix trains Wren on the press, passing on her father's craft. Emotional beat: urgency braided with tenderness; teaching as legacy.

chapters.title: Crane's Summons
chapters.summary: Tamsin is summoned before Crane, who lays out evidence of their tampering — real or staged? Tamsin walks a razor's edge, confessing to a lesser sin to conceal a greater. Emotional beat: cold sweat performance; survival by partial truth.

chapters.title: The Shop Is Watched
chapters.summary: Soldiers loiter across the lane from the print shop. The circle must move the plates through the city unnoticed. Beatrix devises a plan: hide the archive inside a shipment of funeral monuments' rubbings. Emotional beat: grim ingenuity; mourning as camouflage.

chapters.title: Funeral Procession
chapters.summary: The plates travel in a coffin amid a staged mourner's procession, Beatrix playing chief griever. A checkpoint nearly unravels everything until Tamsin, in uniform, waves them through. Emotional beat: collective held breath; complicity sealed in ritual.

chapters.title: Safe House on Tanner's Row
chapters.summary: The archive rests in a tannery cellar. Beatrix finally reads the full account — atrocities her father documented, names of the disappeared. Emotional beat: devastation and clarity; this is why the truth must outrun the historians.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Offered promotion and transfer away from Vellham, Tamsin must decide whether to remain a functionary or become a fugitive. They burn their own census originals. Emotional beat: identity shed like a uniform; freedom and homelessness in one act.

chapters.title: The Ice Groans
chapters.summary: The river cracks audibly; bargemen say days remain. But Crane has ordered the port sealed pending 'historical review.' Every exit is watched. Emotional beat: closing walls versus breaking ice; despair met with stubbornness.

chapters.title: Fire as Diversion
chapters.summary: The circle sets a controlled fire in an empty warehouse to draw the garrison. Wren insists on lighting it herself, redeeming her earlier mistake. Emotional beat: sacrifice and redemption; the city's own chaos turned to cover.

chapters.title: Loading the Barge
chapters.summary: Under smoke and confusion, the plates are rowed to a coal barge bribed with the last of the circle's money. Beatrix stays ashore to finish one final printing. Emotional beat: frantic hope; letting go of the thing you saved.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Beatrix prints fifty copies of the true account on her father's press, knowing the shop cannot be saved. She sets her own name beneath his for the first time. Emotional beat: catharsis; claiming authorship of her life and the record.

chapters.title: Crane at the Door
chapters.summary: Crane arrives personally as the press cools. He and Beatrix face each other over the finished stack — he offers mercy again; she offers him a copy. 'History will find you,' he warns. Emotional beat: chilling standoff; conviction against institution.

chapters.title: The Burning of Eastwick's
chapters.summary: Soldiers torch the shop. Beatrix watches her childhood burn, the press bell cracking in the heat like a dying bell. Tamsin pulls her back from the flames. Emotional beat: total loss transformed into liberation; nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: The river shatters open with a sound like cannon fire. The barge slips downstream through the floes, carrying the archive toward sympathetic printers in the low country. Emotional beat: awe and release; nature itself declaring the deadline met.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix, Tamsin, and Wren regroup among the ruins. Crane's men arrest stragglers, but the circle scatters along planned routes, each carrying copies sewn into clothing. Emotional beat: exhausted gratitude; survival as the first victory.

chapters.title: The Record Travels
chapters.summary: Episodic glimpses: a copy read aloud in a canal-side tavern; a typesetter in another city recognizing Eastwick's typeface and weeping. Emotional beat: the archive taking root beyond its makers; memory proving portable.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Carries
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin reflects on the census lists they once filed and the ones they burned, deciding to write their own account — the story of the counters as well as the counted. Emotional beat: reconciliation with complicity; authorship as penance.

chapters.title: A New Case of Type
chapters.summary: Months later, in the low country, Beatrix apprentices at a small press, teaching Wren the trade properly this time. Word arrives that Crane has been dismissed — the record surfaced where it could not be suppressed. Emotional beat: cautious joy; the long game won.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Beatrix travels to a riverside town where the full account is being reprinted openly. She watches strangers read her father's words and her name beneath them. Emotional beat: belonging achieved not by blood or place, but by contribution; inheritance fulfilled.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Moving
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Beatrix's POV. Standing on the new town's docks, she posts the first page of the true account publicly, then turns back to the press. The river runs high and free. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory entrusted forward, the story continuing without her guarding it.
